sections.heading: Working today
intro: All of this is covered by the offline suite — **1,871 tests, 1,820 passing, 0 failing, 51 skipped**. The 51 skipped need a real model; they all pass through the `claude-cli` backend (see below), and have not been run against the API for want of credit. The newest of them is why-not-just-what — "i'm trying to save money" written down as a stated reason with his own words on it, and the cheaper-but-further flat then coming back as the pick with the reason said out loud, on that backend on 2026-10-06. Before it, the hard line — six sentences seeking help toward harm refused before any model turn, seven innocent ones passed, two crisis messages read as crisis, one thread read for where it was going, and the whole path from a test number, all on that backend on 2026-10-06 (see the first rule under "The rules it keeps"). Before it, "where were we?" — a job mid-flight, asked for an update, answered with what is done before what is left before the one thing it needs, which is the difference between a status update and a demand. It passed twice on that backend on 2026-10-06. Next to it are the subscription flows — a year of receipts sorted into subscriptions and not-subscriptions, a `cancelling` row answered as not-yet rather than done, and a cancellation walked to the last button and pressed only on a real yes — on that backend the same day.
Newest first. One line each; open the fold for what is actually proved and what is not.

sections.heading: Built, but never run against the real thing
intro: Written carefully, offline-tested, and **unproven**. Do not treat any of it as working. `docs/unverified.md` is the full ledger, test by test. Newest first.

sections.heading: Not connected, and what you have to supply
intro: Reason says all of this itself when asked: the `capabilities` tool and `account_list` report every one of these as not connected, with what is missing. It starts up fine with none of them. Newest first; the fold is what you must supply.
outro: Picked, and genuinely not started: Reason's own email address, real bookings and checkouts with the exact total approved, group texts with polls, decks, and plug-in apps. `docs/features.md` has the agreed order under **Decided 2026-10-04**.

usecases.name: Nobody uses it to hurt anybody
usecases.hook: every text screened before the model; harm gets no turn at all
usecases.detail: A separate narrow model call reads every message anybody sends, with the last few lines of the thread, before the model sees it. On **harm** — planning or carrying out violence, a weapon, a bomb, a poison, a nerve agent, drugging somebody, stalking, anything sexual involving a child, breaking into accounts; whatever the framing — there is no model turn: a refusal written in code goes back, the thread keeps it, and it is a ledger row and a strike. Three strikes in a day pause that person and tell the master the count and the kind, never the words. Borderline reads, a person in crisis, and a screen that could not run all get a turn with every outward tool refused; crisis gets a guaranteed crisis line and never a strike. No off switch.

usecases.name: Why, not just what
usecases.hook: the reason you gave is kept and it reorders the options
usecases.detail: "I want to move" is one job; "to save money" and "for a shorter commute" are two different jobs out of the same five flats. A reason you state is its own row — the subject, the goal in your terms, and **your own sentence, verbatim** — kept apart from facts and from preferences, because a fact is what stays true about you and a reason is what you are trying to achieve. It outlives the task it was said on, arrives on the sheet of every later job on that subject, and the model is told to rank by it and to say so in one short clause. Two things are code's: a reason with no sentence behind it is refused, so an invented motive cannot start sorting your options; and a correction **supersedes** rather than overwrites, so the old one is kept as replaced and stays checkable. It is a goal and never a permission.

usecases.name: Memory you can correct
usecases.hook: numbered sections for everything it holds; text back a correction and it sticks
usecases.detail: "What do you remember about me" is one page with a number on every line: what you told it, what it is **guessing** (labelled as guesses, never said back as fact, and only ever promoted by you saying the thing), what you have turned down and why, **why you said you are doing things**, and what it may do without asking. Text back "#4's wrong, she's my cousin" and it changes that one line — and stops saying the old version anywhere, including in things it has already said.

usecases.name: Taste
usecases.hook: a no is kept in your words and shapes every later pick
usecases.section: What it may do without asking
usecases.detail: When you turn an option down it keeps your reason, in your words, with what kind of no it was, and every later pick is made knowing it. It is a preference and never a permission: nothing it learns this way lets it spend anything or send anything.

usecases.name: Noticing things first
usecases.hook: goes looking in mail and calendar, one catch a day
usecases.detail: It goes looking, every couple of hours, at a connected mailbox and calendar: a meeting that moved deep in a thread, a bill sitting unread, a reply somebody is waiting on. Anything they already handled is checked against the live mailbox and never raised. One unprompted catch a day, counted in the database, one nudge per thing, sent at the moment it is useful rather than in a batch, nothing in their night, and the three-question bar in front of all of it. How much initiative they want is theirs — the moment it matters, one batched line a day, or only ever when they ask — and none of it is permission to act for them. See **Noticing things first** above. The judgement side has only ever been exercised with a fake model: whether its sense of "worth interrupting somebody for" is any good is in `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Subscriptions
usecases.hook: a year of receipts, a monthly total, and a real cancellation
usecases.detail: Read a year of their receipts and come back with what is actually going out, keep the list, show it as a page with a monthly total, and cancel one — on the web with their own saved sign-in, or as a written request from their own address. Both behind their explicit yes, and nothing is ever called cancelled until something confirms it. See **Subscriptions** above.

usecases.name: Their Drive
usecases.hook: find a file, read a Doc, Sheet, Slides or a real PDF
usecases.detail: Against the same fake Google: find a file by its name or by what is inside it, read a Doc, a Sheet (first sheet, and it says so), Slides, a text or html file, **and a PDF — read on this machine, against real PDFs built in the tests**, including a real password-protected one that is refused and a real scan that is named as a scan — make a new Google Doc and send back the link. A Word file, an image and a folder each get a plain sentence saying Reason cannot read that one, with the link. Nothing is deleted, shared or edited, because the scopes for that are not asked for. And **an existing Google connection is not a Drive connection**: Drive is its own tap, and asking for it adds a permission without costing them the ones they have. Nothing has been sent to Google. See **Their Drive** and `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Reminders and timers
usecases.hook: real turns at real times; fired only once the message is out
usecases.detail: Reminders and timers that fire real turns at real times. **A timer counts as fired once its message is in the outbox, not before**: a turn that throws or times out leaves it due, it is tried again on the next sweep (three tries in all, `REASON_TIMER_MAX_ATTEMPTS`), the reply goes out under a key that belongs to that timer so retrying cannot text twice, and if it still cannot be got out they get one line saying a reminder was missed and what it was. Until 2026-10-06 the timer was marked fired first, and a turn killed after the Mac slept took the reminder with it — not sent, not retried, nobody told. `Runtime.tick`, pinned by `test/timer-claim.test.js`.

usecases.name: Gmail, per person and as many accounts as they have
usecases.hook: read, send, bin across every account, attached PDFs included
usecases.detail: Against a fake Google server built from their docs: a link each person taps, tokens stored and refreshed against their own conversation and their own address, reading across every account they connected with each result labelled, sending and binning gated on the real recipients, the whole body **and the sending account**, an email's own words treated as data and never as an instruction, and a dead connection reported as needing a reconnect rather than retried. **A PDF attached to an email is read** — against real PDFs built in the tests and really put through this machine's own reader — with the bytes fetched only for the one file asked about, a real scan named as a scan, a really encrypted one refused, and an instruction written inside the document flagged and unable to become a yes. Nothing has been sent to Google — the client id and secret are on the machine and have deliberately never been used. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: A message Reason starts reaches the phone
usecases.hook: reminders and task news go to the thread, not the log
usecases.detail: A reminder, a task's news, a watcher or a picked-up thread goes to the thread that conversation lives in. Until 2026-10-05 these had no channel and were printed into the server's log instead — written, recorded as said, and never texted. `src/deliver.js`, pinned by `test/deliver.test.js`.

usecases.name: Research, with a real pick
usecases.hook: many searches, sources read in full, then a recommendation
usecases.detail: Several different searches, the best sources read in full, a source log of what each one said and when, then a recommendation with what would change it. Capped so one question cannot run away, and it says when a cap cut it short. A big question runs as a durable task. The provider interface and the whole flow are offline-tested against a fake provider and fixture pages; the Tavily request shape is tested against its documented contract but **has never been sent to Tavily** — no key. **Reddit is never fetched** (its robots.txt forbids everyone); what threads say arrives as search snippets, labelled as snippets.

usecases.name: Finding out what is in a video
usecases.hook: a link becomes timestamped lines, and says what produced them
usecases.detail: A YouTube link (and many other video sites) → the title, channel, length, description, chapters and what is in it as timestamped lines. It reads the captions when there are any; a long one is cut and says which stretch is missing, and a follow-up reads that stretch. An age gate, a private video or a region block comes back as the reason. Every result says which of three things produced it, so "watched" is only ever said when something really watched. Proved against real YouTube videos as well as offline fixtures; see the manual checks in `docs/unverified.md`. The **video model** tiers — watching a YouTube link, and transcribing audio from anywhere else — are built and offline-tested but need `GEMINI_API_KEY`. The audio-only download and the delete-after are proved for real; nothing has ever been sent to Google.

usecases.name: Saved sign-ins, site playbooks, a daily spending limit and Spotify
usecases.hook: browsing free, the committing click gated, tokens never shared
usecases.detail: Against local fixture pages and a fake Spotify server: browsing is free, the committing click is gated whatever the site calls it, a changed total asks again, and one person's sign-in or token is never usable from another's conversation. No real site has been signed in to and nothing has been sent to Spotify.

usecases.name: Telling somebody what's new, in passing
usecases.hook: one live thing, one a day, never while a confirm is open
usecases.detail: The gates are code's: nothing unverified is ever put in front of the model, nothing is mentioned that is not live for that person, one thing per reply and one per person per day, never while a confirmation is open, never on a message Reason started, and never to somebody who arrived after the feature did. Marked heard only once the reply really went out. What no test can prove is the part the model owns — whether it actually reads the moment right and writes one casual line rather than a pitch. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Messages arriving the way people actually send them
usecases.hook: two texts are one turn; a photo arrives as a picture
usecases.detail: Two texts seconds apart are one turn; the parts of one iMessage (a pasted link and its preview card) are one message rather than three; a photo or screenshot reaches the model as a picture to look at, and anything that cannot be read is explained once, by name, instead of being called "blank". Against the real failing shapes from a real phone.

usecases.name: Photos, voice notes and links
usecases.hook: HEIC converted, voice transcribed, and a row for each
usecases.section: What they send: photos, voice notes, links
usecases.detail: An iPhone HEIC converted before anything looks at it, a voice note transcribed and answered as the words in it, a link sent as its own bubble, and a row for every one of them saying what was actually got out of it. See **What they send** above.

usecases.name: Tapbacks, screen effects and voice notes
usecases.hook: Sendblue's own grammar and limits checked before any request
usecases.detail: As tools, with Sendblue's own grammar and limits checked before any request — including the awkward part, which is that "exactly one emoji" has to treat a skin tone, a family, a keycap and a flag as one.

usecases.name: A voice, and ears
usecases.hook: says a voice note, listens to one, every failure named
usecases.detail: Reason can say something as a real voice note and listen to one you send, with every failure a named reason. The whole path has run on this machine with the real speech model — spoken, converted, served back and transcribed word for word — but no voice note has been sent to or received from a real phone. See `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Inline replies
usecases.hook: pinned under the message they answer, both directions
usecases.detail: Both ways: a reply pinned under the message it answers, a refused pin that falls back to an ordinary message instead of losing it, and an inbound reply that arrives saying which message it was sent under. Never sent to a real phone — see `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: The Bland adapter
usecases.hook: exact request body and every status mapped; no call placed
usecases.detail: Driven by an injected `fetch` that could not reach the network if it wanted to: the exact request body (`record: true`, the announcement as `first_sentence`, the standing rules ahead of the goal), every one of Bland's call statuses mapped onto Reason's, the audio fetched from Bland's own authenticated endpoint rather than from `recording_url`, and the signed call-finished webhook. No call has been placed.

usecases.name: A keep-by date on everything
usecases.hook: a real export copy and a delete that really deletes
usecases.detail: A keep-by date on everything, with an export that is a real copy and a delete that is a real delete. See **Your data**.

usecases.name: An account per person
usecases.hook: fully separate, master-approved by text, a daily limit each
usecases.section: Everyone who texts it gets their own Reason
usecases.detail: Fully separate, with the master approving each one by text — and a daily limit each, so nobody can run up the bill.

usecases.name: Follow-ups
usecases.hook: a quiet plan with open questions is picked back up
usecases.detail: When a plan with open questions goes quiet for hours, Reason picks it back up on its own — at most once per plan per day, twice per conversation.

usecases.name: Pages
usecases.hook: an answer at a link, reopened and updated at the same one
usecases.detail: Made, updated at the same link, opened by the owner's own link with nothing to type, closed to the bare link until shared, shareable on request through a separate read-only link, with a tapped answer coming back as one event turn. Against the HTTP handler, no browser needed.

usecases.name: Phone calls
usecases.hook: announcement, recording, caps — as far as no account goes
usecases.detail: As far as they can go without an account: the provider interface, the recorded announcement, the recording store, the audio arriving with the summary in one message, the never-pay-by-phone guard, and the per-person daily caps on calls and on call minutes. Against a fake provider that dials nothing.

usecases.name: `npm run serve`
usecases.hook: the long-running process with its sweep and webhook listener
usecases.detail: The long-running process with its sweep and webhook listener.

usecases.name: The confirm gate, the action ledger and the accounts registry
usecases.hook: "what did you do today" is read off a table, never memory
usecases.detail: The **confirm gate**, the **action ledger** ("what did you do today" is read off a table, never from memory), and the **connected-accounts registry**.

usecases.name: Export and delete
usecases.hook: call recordings and pages included, off disk too
usecases.detail: Export and delete, call recordings and pages included.

usecases.name: A real browser
usecases.hook: it drives itself; the commit click always needs your yes
usecases.detail: A real browser it drives itself: open a page, read it, click, fill a form, screenshot. One profile per conversation so logins stick between turns. The final commit click always needs your explicit yes.

usecases.name: Reading one web page
usecases.hook: answering from what the page actually says
usecases.detail: Reading one web page and answering from what it actually says.

usecases.name: Plans
usecases.hook: make, change any detail, lock, cancel, mark done
usecases.detail: Make one, change any detail, lock it, cancel it, mark it done. It tracks what is still open and will not lock while something is.

usecases.name: Tasks that outlive a message
usecases.hook: a row with a goal, a wake time and a progress log
usecases.detail: Chasing someone, waiting on a reply, a multi-step errand. A row in the database with a goal, a next wake time and a progress log, so killing the process loses nothing. Reason only speaks about one when something actually changed.

usecases.name: Watchers
usecases.hook: watch a page, come back when one thing changes
usecases.detail: Watch a page, come back when a specific thing changes on it.

usecases.name: Memory about people
usecases.hook: facts and preferences, read back whole, or forgotten
usecases.detail: Facts, preferences, who someone is; read it all back, or forget a person outright.

usecases.name: Cancelling a subscription
usecases.hook: fifteen services' flows read off their help pages, none walked
usecases.detail: The registry in `src/cancel-routes.js` was read off fifteen services' own help pages on 2026-10-06 and **not one of those flows has been walked**. No account here has ever been cancelled and nothing in Reason has ever pressed one of those buttons: the web rail is proved end to end against a fixture service on 127.0.0.1 (a sign-in, a retention offer, a two-step cancellation, a confirmation number), and the mail rail against the fake Google. On 2026-10-06 that fixture rail was also walked by the **real model**, unaided: it read the retention offer and said so, clicked past it, stopped at "Finish Cancellation", said the $5 fee and the end date back, asked, and pressed only after a yes in his own words. What a fixture cannot settle is whether Netflix's page still says "Finish Cancellation", whether any of these sites will talk to an automated browser at all, and whether a retention wall sits somewhere the registry does not know about. Four of the entries do not document their last button and say so; one could not be read at all and is `unknown`.

usecases.name: The Bland call provider
usecases.hook: written from their docs, field by field; no phone has rung
usecases.detail: Written from Bland's own docs (`POST /v1/calls`, `GET /v1/calls/{id}`, `GET /v1/calls/{id}/recording`, their webhook-signing page), read 2026-10-05, with the page named next to every field in `src/calls/bland.js`. There is no `BLAND_API_KEY` on this machine, so **no phone has ever rung**: 38 tests drive it with an injected `fetch` and assert on the exact URL and body. What only a real call can settle — that the opening line is really spoken word for word, that it really declines when asked for a card, that a recording really comes back, that a webhook really arrives — is all listed in `docs/unverified.md`.

usecases.name: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.hook: one real one-step hand-over ran; everything harder has not
usecases.section: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.detail:
**One real hand-over has run end to end**, and that is the whole of it. 59 offline tests cover the switch, the master-only gate, the brief, what is read back off disk, the states, the pages, the quiet window and the delete; none of them start a process. On 2026-10-05 one real job was handed to a real `openclaw` session against a scratch data dir: the detached runner started, the builder read the brief and appended `progress`, `detail` and `done` lines in the shapes it was asked for, the sentinel landed with exit 0, the reply parsed out of the real envelope, the state settled to `done` from what the builder wrote, and both pages built. So the path works once, for a one-step job.

What has **not** been run: a job long enough to be swept while mid-turn, a builder asking a question and the answer getting back to it, a risky action going through the gate to a real builder, two jobs at once, a restart mid-build, and the text itself (no channel is connected on this machine). Every state and page for all of those is offline-tested and none of them is proven.

usecases.name: The video model
usecases.hook: request shape pinned header for header; nothing sent to Google
usecases.detail: `src/gemini.js`, written from Google's current docs (POST to `models/<model>:generateContent`, a YouTube URL as `file_data.file_uri`, a time range as `video_metadata.start_offset`/`end_offset`, and for audio the Files API's two-step resumable upload then `file_data` with a `mime_type`). There was no `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the environment when this was written, so **nothing has ever been sent to Google** — it has only answered an injected fetch. The tests pin the request shape header for header, which is all that can be checked without a key. The halves either side *are* proved for real: the audio-only download, the file on disk, the deletion afterwards, and the cache spending nothing on a second ask were all run against a real YouTube video. Also unverified: the optional OpenAI transcriber in `src/transcribe.js`, same reason.

usecases.name: Video sites other than YouTube
usecases.hook: `yt-dlp` covers hundreds; only YouTube has been tried
usecases.detail: `yt-dlp` covers hundreds of them and the code treats them all the same, but only YouTube has been tried. Expect the metadata to be thinner elsewhere and captions to be missing more often.

usecases.name: The Linq channel
usecases.hook: iMessage / RCS / SMS from their v3 docs; no key, no text
usecases.detail: Written from Linq's published Partner API v3 docs, signature checking per the webhook spec they document. No key has ever sent a real text.

usecases.name: Sending an attachment over Linq
usecases.hook: their documented pre-upload flow, so a recording rides along
usecases.detail: Their documented pre-upload flow, so a call recording can ride along with the summary. Same caveat: never run.

usecases.name: The API path
usecases.hook: all 25 live tests pass — through claude-cli, not the API
usecases.section: Testing on a Claude subscription (owner only, local)
usecases.detail: All 25 live tests now pass — but through the `claude-cli` backend on a Claude subscription, not through the Anthropic API that Reason actually ships on (there is no credit on this machine). Same prompts, same tools, different backend: no prompt cache, and the CLI owns the tool loop. So the behaviour is proved with a real model; the path it will run on is not. In this repo "live tested" means *via claude-cli*, and `docs/unverified.md` says so test by test.

usecases.name: Whether a real call keeps its promises
usecases.hook: the announcement and the card refusal need a real voice agent
usecases.detail: Code can prove a call request cannot carry payment details and cannot be placed without the recorded announcement. Whether a real voice agent says the announcement first and holds the line when a restaurant pushes for a card is a property of whichever provider gets bought — and it is the first thing to test on the first real call.

usecases.name: Google Drive
usecases.hook: two scopes on the Data Access page, then one tap each
usecases.detail: The same OAuth client, plus **two scopes added on its Data Access page** — `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly` and `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file` — and the **Drive API enabled** on the project. Google rejects an app whose code requests a scope not declared there, so until those two are on the page a Drive connect fails at Google's own screen rather than here. Nothing goes in `.env`: the code side is built. Then **each person taps a Drive link of their own** — connecting Gmail does not connect Drive, so everybody already on needs one more tap, and nobody has to redo their mail. `drive.readonly` is a **restricted** scope, which is the same review class Gmail already put this app in, so it changes the verification work not at all; `drive.file` is non-sensitive. See **Their Drive**.

usecases.name: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.hook: an OpenClaw install plus a flag; off by default on purpose
usecases.section: Handing work to the builders on this machine
usecases.detail: `REASON_REMOTE_BUILD=1` plus an [OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw) install on the same machine (`REASON_OPENCLAW_BIN`, `REASON_OPENCLAW_AGENT`). Off by default on purpose and the master's alone even when on — see **Handing work to the builders on this machine** above. With it off there is no such tool and nobody is told one exists; Reason still writes code for anyone who asks, it just has nobody to hand the running of it to.

usecases.name: Phone calls
usecases.hook: a Bland account at $0.14 a connected minute; caps hold it
usecases.detail: A [Bland](https://app.bland.ai) account, then `REASON_CALL_PROVIDER=bland` and `BLAND_API_KEY`. Their published Start-plan rate is **$0.14 a connected minute**, free to sign up; `REASON_MAX_CALLS_PER_DAY` and `REASON_MAX_CALL_MINUTES_PER_DAY` are what stop one person running that up. Optional: `BLAND_FROM_NUMBER` (without it Bland dials from its own pool), and `BLAND_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from their dashboard so the call-finished webhook is verified by signature rather than only by the unguessable token in its URL. With no `REASON_PUBLIC_URL` there is no webhook at all and outcomes are polled, which Bland's own docs call the right answer rather than a workaround. `docs/call-providers.md` compares the alternatives.

usecases.name: Web search, and therefore research
usecases.hook: a Tavily key; 1,000 free credits is ~200 questions a month
usecases.detail: `TAVILY_API_KEY`, from [app.tavily.com](https://app.tavily.com). **1,000 API credits a month, free, no credit card** (their docs, read 2026-10-05). A basic search costs 1 credit, so that is about 1,000 searches a month, and one research run spends up to 5 of them — roughly 200 questions a month on the free tier. Past it: **$0.008 a credit** pay-as-you-go, or $30/mo for 4,000. Reading the pages afterwards is free (a plain fetch, not a Tavily extract). Without it, `capabilities` says search is not connected, `research` refuses rather than guessing, and Reason reads a page whose address it can name itself and says that is all it did. Brave Search is the alternative and is **not wired**: its free tier is $5 of monthly credit on a billing plan.

usecases.name: Watching a video, or reading one with no captions
usecases.hook: a Gemini key; ~0.45 cents a minute to watch
usecases.detail: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, from aistudio.google.com. Per Google's docs (2026-10-05): a video is ~100 tokens per second at default media resolution, audio is 32 tokens per second, so on `gemini-3.8-flash` at $0.75 / M input that is roughly **0.45 cents a minute to watch** and **0.14 cents a minute to listen**, plus output. Free tier capped at 8 hours of YouTube a day. Public videos only. Capped at `REASON_VIDEO_MAX_MINUTES` (60) a video and cached per video and tier. No ffmpeg needed. Without it, a caption-less video comes back saying there is no way to know what is in it, and Reason says that.

usecases.name: Videos at all
usecases.hook: just `yt-dlp` on the machine — no key, no account
usecases.detail: Nothing but `yt-dlp` on the machine (`pipx install yt-dlp`, `brew install yt-dlp`, or the standalone binary), or `REASON_YTDLP_BIN` pointed at it. No key, no account. It is what fetches a video's details, its captions and its audio, so with it missing there is nothing Reason can find out about any video — and the tool and `capabilities` both say so.

usecases.name: Listening to a voice note
usecases.hook: a Gemini key plus afconvert, or ffmpeg on Linux
usecases.section: What they send: photos, voice notes, links
usecases.detail: `GEMINI_API_KEY`, plus `/usr/bin/afconvert` (part of macOS) or `ffmpeg` on the PATH — on Linux that means installing ffmpeg.

usecases.name: An iPhone photo (HEIC)
usecases.hook: nothing on a Mac; on Linux it is refused honestly instead
usecases.section: What they send: photos, voice notes, links
usecases.detail: Nothing on a Mac — `/usr/bin/sips` is part of the OS. **On Linux there is nothing to supply:** the conversion is sips and has no fallback, so an iPhone photo is refused honestly rather than read.

usecases.name: Google verification (no "unverified app" screen)
usecases.hook: Google's own review; nothing in `.env` makes it go away
usecases.detail: Nothing in `.env` makes this go away: it is Google's review of the project, done in the Cloud console by the project owner. The code side is ready — public home, privacy and terms pages, the Limited Use statement, the narrowest scopes, an in-product notice with every link, and `GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION` for Search Console. What is left is a domain the owner controls (the Tailscale name counts as Tailscale's), Search Console, a demo video, the scope justifications, and for Gmail a paid annual security assessment. Step by step in `docs/google-verification.md`.

usecases.name: Spotify
usecases.hook: a developer app and a redirect URI; Premium to play
usecases.detail: A developer app from [developer.spotify.com/dashboard](https://developer.spotify.com/dashboard): put its id and secret in `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID` and `SPOTIFY_CLIENT_SECRET`, and add `{REASON_PUBLIC_URL}/spotify/callback` to the app's Redirect URIs. Then each person taps the link Reason sends and approves on Spotify's own page. Playing, pausing, skipping and queueing need Spotify Premium.

usecases.name: OpenTable, Uber, Lyft, DoorDash, Uber Eats, Amazon, Delta, United, Ticketmaster, Fandango
usecases.hook: you sign in once yourself; six of the ten refuse a browser
usecases.detail: You, signed in once yourself: `npm run signin -- <site>` opens a real window, you sign in, you close it. Reason never sees a password. **Six of the ten refuse an automated browser today** — see "Saved sign-ins and real sites" above for which.

usecases.name: Gmail and Calendar
usecases.hook: a Web application OAuth client; no refresh token in `.env`
usecases.detail: A **Web application** OAuth client from the [Google Cloud console](https://console.cloud.google.com/auth/clients), with the Gmail and Calendar APIs enabled on the project: put its id and secret in `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET`, and add `{REASON_PUBLIC_URL}/google/callback` to its Authorized redirect URIs, exactly — scheme, case and trailing slash all have to match. **No refresh token goes in `.env`**: that was the old shape, from before each person had their own Reason, and one refresh token there would mean everybody who texted reached the same inbox. Each person taps the link Reason sends and agrees on Google's own page, and their refresh token is stored against their conversation **and the address Google reported for it**, so one person can connect several Google accounts and each keeps its own grant. While the consent screen is in Testing, only listed test users can connect and Google expires each connection after 7 days. Published and unverified, the cap is 100 **Google accounts** over the project's lifetime, not 100 people — see **Their email**.

usecases.name: Texting
usecases.hook: Sendblue's four values, your own number, a webhook
usecases.detail: Sendblue: `SENDBLUE_API_KEY_ID`, `SENDBLUE_API_SECRET_KEY`, `SENDBLUE_FROM_NUMBER`, `SENDBLUE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (or, superseded, Linq: `LINQ_API_KEY`, `LINQ_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `LINQ_FROM_NUMBER`), plus `REASON_OWNER_NUMBER` set to your own number and a webhook subscription pointed at your host.

usecases.name: Page links that open on a phone
usecases.hook: the address this listener is reachable at
usecases.detail: `REASON_PUBLIC_URL`, the address this listener is reachable at. Pages work without it; their links just only open on this machine, and Reason says so.

usecases.name: A server to run on
usecases.hook: a persistent disk, 1–2 GB, and the data dir pointed at it
usecases.detail: A host with a persistent disk and 1–2 GB of memory, plus `REASON_DATA_DIR` pointed at the mounted volume. See **Running it on a server**.

usecases.name: Payments
usecases.hook: one key, and nothing spends without it
usecases.detail: `REASON_PAYMENTS_KEY`.

usecases.name: The model
usecases.hook: an Anthropic key with credit; everything needs this
usecases.detail: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, with credit. Everything needs this, and a hosted install cannot use the subscription backend instead.
